proposals.name: Broad-industry growth and distress-adjusted EBITDA peers
proposals.mechanism: EV/EBITDA rises with expected growth and with returns on reinvested capital, and it rises mechanically when EBITDA is temporarily depressed, which shows up as high net debt to EBITDA. Matching on these drivers inside the 2-digit industry, with a median over a larger peer set, should keep the industry's risk profile and cut the noise that the earlier harmonic mean of 10 peers added.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.330 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with coverage above 99%.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.75, roic 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Margin-matched sales multiple within broad industry
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so the margin is the main driver of a sales multiple, and growth adds to it. Peers in the same 2-digit industry with similar margins and growth should share the sales multiple far better than peers matched on ROIC and size, and using the median guards against the right-skewed tail that hurt the mean.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.560 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Narrow industry, margin and growth matched EBITDA peers
proposals.mechanism: The tight sales-growth band shrank peer sets to noisy samples. Inside the 3-digit industry, growth and EBITDA margin are better used for ranking than for screening: low-margin firms often carry cyclically depressed EBITDA and higher multiples, and fast growers deserve higher multiples. A median of 20 near neighbours keeps the industry anchor while adjusting for these drivers.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.333 (no worse than the industry median) and beats it in at least 2 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, ebitda_margin 0.75 | k=20, median, min_peers=3 | fallback [same industry_l2]

proposals.name: Cross-industry profitability twins for sales multiples
proposals.mechanism: Sales multiples differ across firms mainly because of profitability (gross margin captures pricing power, EBITDA margin captures cash conversion) and growth, not because of SIC codes, which are coarse. Ranking the whole market on these economic drivers tests whether economic twins beat industry peers, and a median of 20 keeps the estimate robust.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.580 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 1, gross_margin 0.5, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=20, median, min_peers=3

proposals.name: Margin-band industry peers ranked by growth
proposals.mechanism: Peers can only share a sales multiple if they turn sales into profit at similar rates, so a hard EBITDA-margin band of 5 points inside the 2-digit industry enforces that condition directly. Within that set, growth and size explain what is left of the multiple. The 4-digit filter and the mean, which made the sets small and the estimates skewed, are dropped.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.570 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with coverage above 98%.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [same industry_l2]

proposals.name: Leverage and size adjusted industry EBITDA peers
proposals.mechanism: Inside an industry, net debt to EBITDA flags firms whose EBITDA is temporarily low relative to their capital base, and those firms trade at higher EV/EBITDA. Size adds the lower risk premium of larger firms. Ranking on these two features inside the 3-digit industry, with a median of 20 peers instead of a harmonic mean of 12, should adjust the industry median without adding small-sample noise.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.330 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank net_debt_to_ebitda 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=20, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_growth_roic
proposals.mechanism: In a discounted-cash-flow view the EV/EBITDA multiple rises with expected growth and with the return earned on reinvested capital, because high-ROIC growth needs less reinvestment per unit of EBITDA. Peers in the same 3-digit industry with similar growth and ROIC should share the risk, growth and reinvestment profile that drives the multiple.
proposals.prediction: Median absolute log error below the L3 industry-median baseline (0.333) pooled over FY2016-2019, and lower in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_margin_capex
proposals.mechanism: EBITDA ignores capital spending, so firms that must spend heavily on capex turn less EBITDA into free cash flow and should trade at lower EV/EBITDA. Matching on capex intensity and EBITDA margin within the industry aligns the EBITDA-to-free-cash-flow conversion rate across peers.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median absolute log error at or below 0.333, with the largest gain over the industry median in capital-intensive 2-digit SIC groups (manufacturing, energy, utilities).
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, capex_intensity 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_size_leverage
proposals.mechanism: Larger firms are more diversified and easier to finance, so investors demand a lower discount rate and pay higher multiples; high net leverage signals financial risk and limited debt capacity, which lowers the enterprise multiple. Same-industry peers matched on size and net debt to EBITDA should share a similar cost of capital.
proposals.prediction: Beats the warranted-multiple peers baseline (0.380) in all 4 exploration years and comes within 0.02 of the L3 industry median pooled.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank log_sales 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 1 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: SALES_margin_growth
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so differences in profitability are the main reason firms in an industry trade at different sales multiples, and growth adds the forward-looking part. Peers matched on EBITDA margin and sales growth should share both the current earnings per dollar of sales and its expected path.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median absolute log error at least 0.10 below the L3 industry-median baseline (0.603), and lower in all 4 exploration years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: SALES_margin_roic
proposals.mechanism: A dollar of sales is worth more when it produces more operating profit and when the capital behind it earns a high return, because value creation depends on spreads over the cost of capital. Matching EBITDA margin and ROIC within the industry captures both current profitability and how efficiently capital is used.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median absolute log error below 0.55, beating the L3 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, roic 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: SALES_grossmargin_growth
proposals.mechanism: Gross margin reflects pricing power and the business model (for example software or branded goods versus distribution or commodities), which persists longer than operating margin and shows long-run profit potential even for firms that are currently spending heavily on growth. Combined with sales growth, it identifies peers the market expects to earn similar long-run margins per dollar of revenue.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3 industry median (0.603) in at least 3 of 4 years, with the largest gains in high-R&D industries where current EBITDA margins understate long-run profitability.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L2 peers matched on EBITDA-to-cash conversion drivers
proposals.mechanism: My view is that EV/EBITDA is mostly a capitalized growth-and-reinvestment ratio: two firms with the same EBITDA are worth the same only if they grow alike and need the same capex to sustain it, which is what ROIC and capex intensity capture. A broad 2-digit industry keeps the risk and accounting environment comparable while leaving a big enough pool to find close matches on these drivers, which I think a narrow L3 median cannot do. This is the direction I would push hardest on.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3 industry-median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, with a pooled median of 0.32 or lower.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Narrow industry, size-and-growth nearest, harmonic mean
proposals.mechanism: Within a 4-digit-ish SIC 3 industry, firms share products and cost structures, so the remaining dispersion in EV/EBITDA comes mostly from scale (diversification, lower risk) and near-term growth. Taking the nearest peers on those two dimensions and using the harmonic mean, which is the right average for price ratios and damps high-multiple outliers, should tighten the plain industry median. I think this is the safest, most transferable improvement over the baseline.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with a smaller mean |ln error| than the 0.513 baseline because the harmonic mean limits overvaluation tails.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank log_sales 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Cross-industry fundamental twins for EV/EBITDA
proposals.mechanism: This tests whether fundamentals beat SIC codes outright: if EV/EBITDA is driven by growth, reinvestment needs, returns on capital and leverage-related risk, then the nearest firms on those features anywhere in the economy should share the multiple even across industry lines. SIC codes are coarse and stale for many firms, so I expect this to help most for conglomerates and firms in thin industries. It is a riskier bet, but if it works it tells us industry membership is just a noisy proxy.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| within 0.02 of the L3 industry median or better, and lower error than the baseline for targets whose L3 industry has fewer than 10 firms.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | rank capex_intensity 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=20, median, min_peers=3

proposals.name: Margin-matched EV/Sales within L2
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is essentially EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so the single biggest reason two firms in the same industry have different sales multiples is profitability; ignoring margin is why the industry-median EV/Sales error is nearly twice the EBITDA error. Ranking 2-digit industry peers heavily on EBITDA margin, with growth and size as secondary, should remove most of that dispersion. I think this is the highest-payoff direction for EV/Sales.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| at least 0.08 below the L3 industry-median EV/Sales baseline (0.603) in every one of the 4 exploration years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 3, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Cross-industry margin-and-growth peers for EV/Sales
proposals.mechanism: If margin and growth explain most of EV/Sales, the industry screen may be throwing away better-matched firms elsewhere; a high-margin, fast-growing firm should look like other high-margin, fast-growing firms regardless of SIC code. Gross margin adds information on pricing power and operating leverage beyond EBITDA margin, and capex intensity separates asset-heavy from asset-light models with similar margins. I see this as the EV/Sales counterpart to the cross-industry EBITDA test.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3 industry-median EV/Sales baseline in at least 3 of 4 years, and its pooled median is no more than 0.03 worse than the within-L2 margin-matched recipe.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 3, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=3

proposals.name: Industry plus hard EBITDA-margin band for EV/Sales
proposals.mechanism: A hard band on EBITDA margin guarantees every peer has nearly the same profitability per dollar of sales, so their EV/Sales should differ only by growth and size, which the ranking then handles. Keeping the industry screen first preserves similar business risk, and the fallbacks widen industry before giving up on it, keeping the margin constraint throughout. I prefer this as a transparent, rule-based alternative to the weighted-distance version in case the soft weighting under-matches margin.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.55 pooled and below the L3 industry-median baseline in all 4 exploration years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank log_sales 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=3 | fallback [same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.03]

proposals.name: L3 growth-and-return tilt, wide median
proposals.mechanism: In a DCF, EV/EBITDA rises with expected growth and with the return earned on reinvestment, and falls when more of EBITDA has to be spent on capex. Restricting to 3-digit industry peers holds risk and business model roughly fixed, and ranking on growth, ROIC and capex intensity picks the peers whose value drivers match the target. Using k=15 with a median keeps the industry median's robustness, so the tilt adds signal without adding much small-sample noise.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.330 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Margin-matched EV/Sales within L2
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so firms with similar margins should have similar sales multiples once the industry is held broadly fixed. Ranking mainly on EBITDA margin, with gross margin and growth as secondary terms, inside the 2-digit industry addresses margin differences that the plain industry median ignores. A median removes the right-skew that hurt the mean-based versions.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.560, beating the industry median (0.603) in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 1, gross_margin 0.5, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: L3 profitability-and-size neighbours, harmonic
proposals.mechanism: The narrow 10-point growth band threw away too many good industry peers. Dropping it and ranking softly on EBITDA margin and size within the 3-digit industry finds peers with a similar margin of safety and similar scale-related risk. The harmonic mean puts less weight on peers with very high multiples, whose EBITDA is temporarily depressed.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.335 and beats the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 0.5, log_assets 0.5 | k=20, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Margin and capital-intensity EV/Sales within L3
proposals.mechanism: For a given industry, a firm's sales multiple depends on how much of each sales dollar becomes operating profit and on how much capital it takes to produce those sales. Low-turnover, high-margin businesses trade at high EV/Sales. Ranking on EBITDA margin and asset turnover replaces debt-to-assets, which matters little because EV already includes debt.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.570 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, asset_turnover 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Hard margin band EV/Sales with growth ranking
proposals.mechanism: Because EV/Sales scales almost proportionally with margin, requiring peers to be within 5 margin points removes most of the spread in sales multiples. Ranking on growth and gross margin then handles the remaining differences in expected profit growth and pricing power. Falling back to a margin band across all industries keeps the main driver matched even when the industry is thin.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.550 and beats the industry median in all 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank sales_growth_1y 0.5, gross_margin 0.5, log_sales 0.3 | k=10, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [same industry_l2]

proposals.name: L3 growth, leverage and size, trimmed
proposals.mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, EV/EBITDA differences come mainly from growth expectations, and from leverage and size, which proxy for distress risk and the cost of capital. Ranking on these three drivers with a wide k=20 and a trimmed mean keeps the central peers and discards extreme multiples. Matching on capex alone, as the earlier version did, missed this.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.335 and beats the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 0.5, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=20, trimmed_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L3_growth_return_peers
proposals.mechanism: Within an industry, EV/EBITDA differs across firms mainly because of expected growth and the return earned on reinvestment (value driver formula: multiple rises with growth when ROIC exceeds the cost of capital). Choosing same-industry peers that are closest on recent growth, ROIC and reinvestment needs (capex intensity) holds risk roughly fixed and matches the fundamentals that set the multiple.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3/L2 industry median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, and pooled median at or below 0.32.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 2, roic 1.5, capex_intensity 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L2_fundamental_harmonic
proposals.mechanism: A wider 2-digit industry pool lets the ranking find closer fundamental matches on growth, margin quality and leverage while keeping shared industry risk and cyclicality. The harmonic mean of multiples equals the ratio of summed values to summed drivers, which is less biased upward by peers with temporarily depressed EBITDA.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.333 and pooled mean below the 0.513 industry-median baseline, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 2, ebitda_margin 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=10, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: EBITDA_crossindustry_economics
proposals.mechanism: Firms with similar gross margins, growth, capital intensity and returns have similar cash-flow conversion and reinvestment needs, so they should earn similar EV/EBITDA even when their SIC codes differ (SIC codes often misclassify diversified or new-economy firms). A larger k with a trimmed mean averages out idiosyncratic noise from peers that fall outside the industry.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| within 0.02 of the industry median baseline (0.31-0.35), and better than the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple peers (0.380) in all 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | rank gross_margin 1.5, sales_growth_1y 2, capex_intensity 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=15, trimmed_mean, min_peers=3

Ranking 2-digit industry peers mostly by EBITDA margin, then by growth and gross margin, removes most of that variation.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below the EV/Sales industry median baseline (0.603) by at least 0.08 when pooled, and lower in all 4 exploration years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 3, sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Sales_margin_band_crossindustry
proposals.mechanism: Requiring peers to have EBITDA margins within 5 percentage points of the target's fixes the profit conversion of each sales dollar, which is the dominant driver of EV/Sales. Ranking within that band on gross margin, growth and size then matches business-model and risk similarity, and the harmonic mean limits the pull of peers with very high multiples.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.55 and below the industry median baseline in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1.5, log_sales 0.5, ebitda_margin 1 | k=10, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.1] -> []

proposals.name: Sales_L3_profit_growth_return
proposals.mechanism: Close industry peers (3-digit SIC) share cost structures and risk, and within them the sales multiple scales with operating margin, growth and the return on invested capital that makes growth valuable. Matching on these three drivers and averaging with a trimmed mean should give stable, unbiased sales multiples.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.56 and pooled mean below the 0.837 warranted-multiple baseline.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 2.5, sales_growth_1y 1.5, roic 1 | k=6, trimmed_mean, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L2_growth_return_size
proposals.mechanism: Holding cash-flow risk roughly constant within a 2-digit industry, an EV/EBITDA multiple capitalizes expected growth and the return earned on reinvested capital, while size proxies for risk and liquidity. Ranking broad-industry peers on growth, ROIC and size picks firms whose fundamentals imply the same capitalization rate, and the median protects against outliers.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3/L2 industry-median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, with a pooled median of 0.32 or less.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.75, ebitda_margin 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L3_reinvestment_leverage
proposals.mechanism: Two firms with equal EBITDA are worth different amounts if one must spend much more of it on capex or carries more net debt, which raises equity risk and the cost of capital. Within a 3-digit industry, matching on capex intensity, net leverage and growth selects peers with the same conversion of EBITDA into free cash flow and similar risk.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| at least 0.01 lower than the L3/L2 industry median, and lower than the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple peers (0.380) in all 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank capex_intensity 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.75, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L4_nested_fallback_growth
proposals.mechanism: The closest product-market peers share demand shocks, technology and investor clientele, so their multiples carry the most information; when a 4-digit group is too thin, step out to 3- and 2-digit groups instead of pooling unrelated firms. A light growth-and-profitability ranking inside the narrow group removes peers at a different life-cycle stage.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years; the gain should be concentrated among firms whose 4-digit group has at least 5 members.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 0.75, log_assets 0.5 | k=6, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Sales_L2_margin_matched

Ranking 2-digit industry peers mainly on EBITDA margin, then gross margin and growth, picks firms that turn a dollar of sales into similar cash flow and should therefore share the same sales multiple.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| at least 0.08 below the L3/L2 industry-median EV/Sales baseline (0.603), beating it in all 4 exploration years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.mechanism: Because the sales multiple is mostly a function of margin and growth, a firm with a 25% EBITDA margin is better compared with other 25%-margin firms in neighbouring industries than with a 5%-margin firm in its own SIC code. A hard margin band followed by ranking on margin, growth and capital intensity builds a fundamentals-based peer group that does not depend on SIC boundaries.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median EV/Sales in at least 3 of 4 years and comes within 0.03 of the industry-filtered margin recipe; it beats that recipe for firms in thin or mixed industries.

proposals.name: Sales_L3_margin_growth_trimmed
proposals.mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, peers that match on EBITDA margin, growth and capex intensity should have nearly the same value per dollar of sales, since these three drive the free cash flow that sales produce. A trimmed mean over a slightly larger set keeps the noise-reducing benefit of averaging while cutting the extreme multiples of distressed or hyped peers.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.55 and better than the L3/L2 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=12, trimmed_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L3 growth-return-leverage EBITDA peers
proposals.mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, EV/EBITDA is driven mainly by expected growth, return on invested capital and financial risk, as in a discounted cash flow model. Ranking same-industry rivals on 1-year growth, ROIC and net leverage picks peers whose cash flows should be capitalized at similar rates.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln(V_est/V)| below the 0.333 industry-median baseline in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=3 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L2 size-margin-growth EBITDA peers, harmonic

Ranking the survivors on growth and size then captures the remaining differences in expected cash-flow growth and risk, and the fallbacks widen the band rather than dropping the margin match.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.580 and beats the industry median in all 4 years.

proposals.name: Deepest-industry median (EBITDA)
proposals.mechanism: 4-digit SIC peers share products, customers and cost structures more closely than 3-digit peers, so their EV/EBITDA should be a closer match whenever the group is large enough to give a stable median. Falling back to L3 and then L2 only when the narrow group has fewer than 6 firms keeps the noise from small groups under control, and leaving out feature ranking avoids the small-sample noise that hurt the earlier size and capex ranking.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.330 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | k=all, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]

proposals.name: L2 fundamentals-matched EV/EBITDA
proposals.mechanism: In a DCF, EV/EBITDA is driven by growth, by the share of EBITDA that has to be reinvested (capex intensity), and by the return on reinvested capital. Peers from the same broad industry that are closest on these drivers should share the target's discount rate and its conversion of EBITDA into free cash flow, so they should share its multiple. Using the 2-digit industry keeps the peer pool large enough for the ranking to do the work.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3/L2 industry-median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of the 4 exploration years, with a pooled median of 0.32 or lower.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: L3 size-growth-leverage EV/EBITDA, harmonic
proposals.mechanism: Within a narrow 3-digit industry, the main remaining differences in EV/EBITDA come from size (larger firms carry lower risk and better liquidity), growth, and leverage (net debt changes the risk of the EV claim). The harmonic mean averages the EBITDA-to-EV yield, which is closer to additive in value terms, and it limits the pull of a few peers with very high multiples.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median on pooled median error, with a smaller mean error (below 0.50) because the harmonic mean resists high-multiple outliers.

proposals.name: Cross-industry economic twins EV/EBITDA
proposals.mechanism: SIC codes are a rough stand-in for economic similarity. Firms in any industry with similar growth, reinvestment needs, returns on capital and gross-margin structure (which reflects pricing power) should have similar value per unit of EBITDA. A larger k with a median keeps the estimate stable when peers come from industries with different noise.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median error within 0.03 of the industry-median baseline (at most 0.36), and better than the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple peers (0.380) in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 1, gross_margin 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=20, median, min_peers=3

proposals.name: L2 margin-matched EV/Sales
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is the EBITDA margin times EV/EBITDA, so the biggest source of EV/Sales error is a mismatch in profitability. Matching first on EBITDA margin and gross margin within the broad industry, and then on growth, lines up both factors of that product.

Ranking within the band on growth and gross margin then captures how long that profitability is likely to last.

Size stands in for risk and market position, which move the discount rate. Peers in the same 3-digit industry with similar EBIT margin and scale should value a dollar of revenue alike.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median error below 0.55, and below both the 0.674 regression baseline and the 0.691 warranted-peer baseline in every exploration year.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebit_margin 1, log_sales 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L3 reinvestment-and-growth peers, median
proposals.mechanism: EBITDA ignores capital expenditure, so firms that must reinvest heavily convert less EBITDA into free cash flow and deserve lower EV/EBITDA, while faster growth and higher returns on capital raise the multiple. Matching on these within the 3-digit industry captures the main cash-flow drivers of the multiple, and the median avoids the downward bias that the harmonic mean imposed on Recipe 1.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error at or below 0.333 (the industry-median baseline), beating it in at least 2 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank capex_intensity 1, sales_growth_1y 1, roic 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L3 margin-matched sales peers, median
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times the EBITDA margin, so within an industry, differences in sales multiples mostly reflect differences in profitability. Choosing same-industry peers with similar EBITDA and gross margins removes the largest source of dispersion, and the median resists the heavy right skew of sales multiples that hurt the mean in Recipe 2.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.603, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, gross_margin 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L3 growth-matched peers, wide k, median
proposals.mechanism: Holding risk roughly constant within an industry, expected growth is the main driver of EV/EBITDA, so peers with similar recent sales growth and size should share the target's multiple. Using a ranking rather than Recipe 3's narrow growth band keeps enough peers, and a wide k with the median keeps the estimate stable.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error at or below 0.335, beating the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=20, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L3 profitability-growth-leverage sales peers
proposals.mechanism: Recipe 4's leverage matching came close to the baseline, but the sales multiple is mainly driven by margin and growth. Ranking same-industry peers mainly on EBITDA margin, then on growth, with a little weight on leverage, matches the cash-flow and capital-structure profile that sets enterprise value per dollar of sales.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.590, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5, debt_to_assets 0.25 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L2 margin-band sales peers
proposals.mechanism: Because EV/Sales is approximately the EBITDA margin times the EBITDA multiple, peers in the same broad industry whose EBITDA margin is within 5 points of the target's should have similar sales multiples. Ranking those peers on gross margin and growth then refines for cost structure and expected expansion. Fallbacks relax first the margin band and then the industry, so coverage is kept.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.603, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> []

proposals.name: Finest-industry median with hierarchical fallback
proposals.mechanism: Firms in the same 4-digit SIC code share products, customers and risk exposures most closely, so their EBITDA multiples should be the most homogeneous. Ranking on accounting features in Recipe 6 added noise, so this recipe uses the median of all 4-digit peers and falls back to 3-digit and then 2-digit industries only when there are too few.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error at or below 0.330, beating the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | k=all, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]

proposals.name: EBITDA_L3_growth_profitability_neighbors
proposals.mechanism: Within an industry, EV/EBITDA is driven by expected growth and the return earned on reinvested capital, because those determine how much future cash flow each dollar of current EBITDA represents. Picking same-industry peers that are closest in growth, ROIC and margin should remove the within-industry spread that the plain industry median ignores.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.333 (industry median baseline) on pooled FY2016-2019 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1.5, roic 1.5, ebitda_margin 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L2_reinvestment_and_leverage
proposals.mechanism: EBITDA ignores capital spending and capital structure, so two firms with equal EBITDA are worth less per dollar when one must reinvest heavily (high capex intensity) or carries more leverage risk. Matching broad-industry peers on capex intensity, net debt/EBITDA, ROIC and growth aligns the parts of value that EBITDA leaves out.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.345 pooled and lower than the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.357) in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank capex_intensity 1.5, net_debt_to_ebitda 1, roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=12, median, min_peers=6 | fallback []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L4_close_peers_harmonic
proposals.mechanism: Firms in the same 4-digit SIC share products, customers and cost structure, so they are the most direct substitutes for investors; a small set of the closest in growth and margin captures that. The harmonic mean is the value-weighted average of multiples and damps the upward bias from a few very richly priced peers.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.333 pooled, with the gain largest for firms whose 4-digit industry has at least 6 members.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, ebitda_margin 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=6, harmonic_mean, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Sales_L2_margin_matched
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is roughly EV/EBITDA times the EBITDA margin, so firms with different margins should trade at very different sales multiples even in the same industry. Ranking broad-industry peers mainly on EBITDA margin, then gross margin and growth, gives peers whose sales convert to cash flow at the same rate.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.55 pooled, beating the industry median (0.603) in all 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 3, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Sales_cross_industry_margin_band
proposals.mechanism: Because the sales multiple mostly reflects how profitable and how fast-growing each sales dollar is, firms with nearly identical EBITDA margins and growth should share a sales multiple whatever their SIC code. A tight margin band across all industries finds these economic twins when the firm's own industry has few comparable-margin members.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.58 pooled and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years; error is lower than the industry median for firms in the top and bottom margin quintiles.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=8 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.1] -> []

proposals.name: Sales_L3_margin_turnover_trimmed
proposals.mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, the sales multiple depends on profitability per sales dollar and on capital intensity: a firm with low asset turnover needs more capital per dollar of sales, which lowers what the sales are worth. Matching on EBITDA margin, gross margin, asset turnover and growth, and using a trimmed mean to drop outlier peers, should give a stable estimate.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.56 pooled and below the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.674) in every year.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 2.5, gross_margin 1, asset_turnover 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, trimmed_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L3 industry peers matched on growth and profitability (EV/EBITDA)
proposals.mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, firms share their main cash-flow risks, but EV/EBITDA still varies with expected growth and how efficiently capital becomes earnings. Picking the industry peers closest on growth, ROIC and size isolates firms whose discount rate and growth profile, and so whose EBITDA capitalization rate, should be nearly the same.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3/L2 industry median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of the 4 exploration years, with a pooled median below 0.32.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, ebitda_margin 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L2 fundamentals neighbors with harmonic mean (EV/EBITDA)
proposals.mechanism: The broader 2-digit group gives a big enough pool to match closely on the drivers of a warranted multiple: growth, return on capital, leverage and size. The harmonic mean averages the earnings yield, not the multiple, so a few peers with temporarily depressed EBITDA and inflated multiples cannot drag the estimate up.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median error below 0.333 and a mean error below the 0.492 warranted-regression baseline; beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_assets 0.5, ebitda_margin 0.5 | k=10, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Leverage-banded L3 peers (EV/EBITDA)
proposals.mechanism: Enterprise value per unit of EBITDA tracks risk, and leverage both signals and causes differences in asset risk and financial-distress costs inside an industry. Requiring similar net debt/EBITDA within the same 3-digit industry, then ranking on growth and capital intensity (the share of EBITDA used up by reinvestment), compares firms with similar risk and similar free-cash-flow conversion.
proposals.prediction: Beats the industry median baseline in at least 2 of 4 years, with the biggest gains among highly levered firms (net debt/EBITDA above 3).
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3, band net_debt_to_ebitda±1.5 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2, band net_debt_to_ebitda±1.5] -> [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]

proposals.name: Margin-banded L3 peers (EV/Sales)
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so firms that turn sales into cash flow at very different rates cannot share a sales multiple, even in the same industry. Restricting peers to the same industry with EBITDA margin within 5 points removes the main reason sales multiples are dispersed, and ranking on growth and gross margin captures how much a dollar of future sales is worth.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median error below 0.50, clearly beating the 0.603 industry median baseline in all 4 exploration years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 0.5 | k=6, median, min_peers=3 | fallback [same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.03] -> [same industry_l2]

proposals.name: Cross-industry profitability twins (EV/Sales)
proposals.mechanism: Once margin, growth and capital efficiency are matched, a dollar of sales should be worth about the same across industries, because value is capitalized cash flow and these features determine the cash flow per dollar of sales and its growth. Dropping the industry screen gives a much larger pool, so the nearest neighbors can be very close on the features that matter most for EV/Sales.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median error below 0.55, beating both the industry median (0.603) and the warranted regression (0.674) in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, asset_turnover 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=3

proposals.name: L2 margin-and-returns neighbors with harmonic mean (EV/Sales)
proposals.mechanism: Within a 2-digit sector, firms with similar EBITDA margins, ROIC and growth should earn similar value per dollar of revenue, because together these set the size, quality and persistence of cash flows. The harmonic mean limits the influence of richly valued outliers that are common in sales multiples, such as pre-profit high-growth names.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median error below 0.55 and mean error below the 0.837 warranted-regression baseline; beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 2, roic 0.5, sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 0.5 | k=8, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L3_growth_return_neighbors
proposals.mechanism: Under a constant-growth DCF, EV/EBITDA rises with expected growth and with how much of EBITDA turns into free cash flow, which depends on return on capital and reinvestment needs. Same-industry firms share risk and accounting conventions. Within that industry, the nearest neighbours on growth, ROIC and capex intensity should share the target's warranted multiple more closely than the industry as a whole.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3/L2 industry-median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, with a pooled median of 0.31 or lower.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L2_cashconversion_harmonic
proposals.mechanism: EBITDA leaves out D&A and R&D reinvestment. Firms with heavy capex or R&D therefore convert less of their EBITDA into free cash flow, or else are buying growth that the market prices. Matching on capex intensity, R&D intensity, EBITDA margin and growth inside a broad 2-digit industry captures this, while keeping the peer pool large enough. The harmonic mean is the standard unbiased way to average price-to-fundamental ratios.
proposals.prediction: Beats the industry-median baseline in at least 3 of 4 years and beats the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.357) in all 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank capex_intensity 1, rnd_intensity 1, ebitda_margin 0.75, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=10, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: EBITDA_crossindustry_fundamental_twins
proposals.mechanism: Value drivers, not SIC codes, set the multiple: growth, profitability, reinvestment intensity and size (a proxy for risk). A fundamental nearest-neighbour match across all industries finds economic twins that SIC codes split apart, for example a software-like firm filed under services. It is a nonparametric form of the warranted multiple that does not assume linearity.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median error below the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple peers baseline (0.380) and within 0.03 of the industry-median baseline. Its errors should be only partly correlated with those of the industry-based recipes.

proposals.name: Sales_L2_margin_matched
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is EV/EBITDA multiplied by EBITDA margin, so margin differences are the main reason EV/Sales varies within an industry. Matching on EBITDA margin and gross margin, a proxy for long-run margin potential, within a 2-digit industry removes that variation. Growth is added as the second-order driver.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| at least 0.08 below the EV/Sales industry-median baseline (0.603) in every exploration year, with a pooled median of 0.52 or lower.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Sales_crossindustry_margin_growth_twins
proposals.mechanism: Firms with the same EBITDA margin, gross margin, growth and R&D intensity have similar cash-flow-per-dollar-of-sales profiles, whatever their SIC code. A cross-industry match on these drivers should beat a single industry median, especially for loss-making or high-R&D firms that are poorly represented in their SIC group.
proposals.prediction: Beats the EV/Sales industry-median baseline (0.603) in all 4 years and beats the Bhojraj-Lee regression (0.674) by at least 0.08 in pooled median.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, rnd_intensity 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5

proposals.name: Sales_L3_margin_band_fallback
proposals.mechanism: Narrow industry peers share business model and capital intensity. A hard ±5pp EBITDA-margin band then ensures that peers earn similar profit per dollar of sales, and ranking on growth and size refines the match within that band. If the band leaves too few peers, the fallbacks widen to the 2-digit industry and then to margin-only matching across all industries, so the margin match survives the fallback.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median below 0.55 and better than the industry-median baseline in at least 3 of 4 years. Coverage should stay close to that of the industry-median baseline.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=6, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [same industry_l2] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.03]

proposals.name: L3 growth-and-reinvestment peers, median
proposals.mechanism: My view is that the last round lost to the industry median mostly because of the aggregator and the peer pool, not the features: harmonic means of 10 peers drawn from a broad L2 pool are pulled around by a few extreme multiples. The value-driver identity EV/EBITDA ~ (1 - g/ROIC)/(WACC - g), adjusted for how much EBITDA must be reinvested, says growth, ROIC and capex intensity are the right things to match on. So I would keep those, but match inside L3 (fallback L2, then all firms), use a larger k and take the median so one odd peer cannot move the estimate.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error at or below 0.330, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years with coverage of at least 99%.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 1 | k=15, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L3 margin-matched EV/Sales, median
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is just EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so for a sales multiple I think profitability is the dominant driver and size barely matters. Recipe 2 matched mostly on ROIC and used a mean, which skewed multiples blow up. I propose matching on EBITDA margin first, gross margin second (pricing power and durability) and growth third, inside L3 with an L2 fallback, and taking the median.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.580, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, gross_margin 0.5, sales_growth_1y 0.3 | k=10, median, min_peers=3 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L3 expensed-investment peers, median
proposals.mechanism: Recipe 3's 10-point growth band threw away too many good peers, so I would drop it. What really separates EV/EBITDA within an industry, in my view, is how much investment runs through the income statement versus the cash-flow statement: heavy R&D spenders show depressed EBITDA and trade at higher multiples, while capex-heavy firms show inflated EBITDA and trade lower. Matching on R&D intensity and capex intensity, with growth as a lighter tiebreaker, and aggregating with the median should line those effects up.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error at or below 0.335, beating the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years, with the largest gains in R&D-heavy industries.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank rnd_intensity 1, capex_intensity 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Asset-turnover and margin EV/Sales peers
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales can be written as (EV/Assets) divided by asset turnover, so a firm's sales multiple depends heavily on how asset-intensive it is, and EBITDA margin then sets how much of those sales turns into value. Recipe 4 matched on leverage, which mainly shifts value between debt and equity and so should barely move EV. I would match on asset turnover and EBITDA margin equally within L2. That pool is wide enough to find close fundamental matches, and the median handles the skew.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.570, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank asset_turnover 1, ebitda_margin 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Industry-free fundamental twins for EV/Sales
proposals.mechanism: This is my exploratory bet. If EV/Sales is really driven by margin, asset intensity, gross margin and growth, then SIC codes, which are notoriously noisy for diversified and newer firms, may be throwing away better peers from other industries. This recipe ranks the whole cross-section on those economic drivers with no industry screen and takes the median of 15 nearest twins. If it beats the industry median, the team should put fundamentals ahead of SIC codes. If it loses, industry membership carries information that accounting ratios do not.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.600 (beating the industry median overall) in at least 3 of 4 years; if it fails, it will fail by more than 0.05.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 1, asset_turnover 0.7, gross_margin 0.5, sales_growth_1y 0.3 | k=15, median, min_peers=3

proposals.name: Finest-industry median with L3/L2 fallback
proposals.mechanism: Recipe 6 ranked on size and capex, and that added noise without adding signal. I think the strongest robust signal for EV/EBITDA is simply membership in a tightly defined industry, where firms share risk, growth outlook and accounting conventions. This recipe takes the median of all 4-digit SIC peers and falls back to L3 and then L2 only when fewer than 6 exist. It is a clean, low-variance test of whether finer industry definitions beat the L3 baseline, which makes it a good candidate for the one-shot holdout.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error between 0.315 and 0.333, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | k=all, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]

Peers in the same 2-digit sector that match on these three drivers share the same cash-conversion and value-creation profile, so they should have similar EBITDA multiples. Size is added with a small weight as a proxy for risk and liquidity.

proposals.mechanism: Firms in the same 3-digit SIC industry share technology, demand cycles and cost of capital. Inside that group, the ones with similar EBITDA margin and growth are at a similar point in the competitive life cycle, so the market should price their EBITDA alike. A small size weight captures the discount for small, riskier firms.

proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

A larger k with a median keeps the estimate stable across the more varied peer set.

proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is roughly EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so differences in margin explain most of the spread in sales multiples. proposals.mechanism: A hard band of +/-5 percentage points of EBITDA margin makes sure no peer has a very different revenue-to-cash conversion, which is the main error source when sales multiples are applied across firms. proposals.name: EBITDA: reinvestment burden and return on capital
proposals.mechanism: EBITDA ignores capex, so a firm that must reinvest heavily turns less of its EBITDA into free cash flow and deserves a lower EV/EBITDA. Matching on capex intensity and ROIC groups firms that turn EBITDA into value at similar rates.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with the biggest gains in capital-intensive 2-digit sectors (utilities, energy, transport).
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank capex_intensity 1, roic 1 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA: size and leverage risk
proposals.mechanism: Larger firms with less leverage have lower and more stable discount rates and less risk of distress, so they support higher multiples of operating earnings. Peers of similar size and similar net debt to EBITDA share the same risk profile, which is what the multiple capitalizes.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.33 pooled over FY2016-2019, and lower mean error than the L3 industry median (0.513).
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank log_assets 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Sales: profitability and growth within 3-digit industry
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is roughly the EBITDA margin times EV/EBITDA, so differences in margin drive most of the spread in sales multiples, and growth drives the rest. Peers matched on EBITDA margin and sales growth should earn similar value per dollar of sales.
proposals.prediction: Median error below the L3 industry-median baseline (0.603) by at least 0.10 in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Sales: gross margin and R&D (intangible business model)
proposals.mechanism: Gross margin shows pricing power and the economics of each extra unit sold. R&D intensity shows how much spending on intangibles is expensed and so pushes current margins below long-run margins. Firms matched on both share a business model and long-run profit potential per dollar of sales, even when current EBITDA margins are misleading.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with the largest gains in tech and healthcare (SIC 28, 35, 36, 38, 73).
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank gross_margin 1, rnd_intensity 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Sales: operating margin and asset intensity
proposals.mechanism: Value per dollar of sales depends on how much profit each dollar earns and how much capital it takes to produce it. Matching on EBIT margin and asset turnover (the two parts of pre-tax ROA) groups firms with similar profitability and capital needs.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.55 pooled over FY2016-2019, beating the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.674) in every year.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebit_margin 1, asset_turnover 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L3_roic_growth
proposals.mechanism: My view is that the strongest lever for EV/EBITDA is the fundamental value-driver pair: a firm's justified multiple rises with growth and with the return it earns on reinvested capital, so peers matched on ROIC and 1-year sales growth inside the 3-digit industry should share the target's multiple more closely than the raw industry median. I'd make this the team's lead direction because it is the textbook Gordon/value-driver logic rather than a data-mined tweak, so it should carry over to unseen years.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3 industry-median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of the 4 exploration years, with pooled median at or below 0.32.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L3_capex_margin
proposals.mechanism: EBITDA ignores the capital needed to sustain it, so two firms with equal EBITDA but different capex intensity generate very different free cash flow; capex-heavy firms should trade at lower EV/EBITDA. Pairing capex intensity with EBITDA margin within the 3-digit industry matches peers on cash conversion and business quality, which I think is the most under-explored angle relative to the standard baselines.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with the largest gains in capital-intensive 2-digit sectors (manufacturing, energy, transport).
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank capex_intensity 1, ebitda_margin 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: EBITDA_L3_size_leverage
proposals.mechanism: Size and leverage proxy for risk and therefore the discount rate: larger firms are more diversified and liquid and command higher multiples, while high net debt to EBITDA signals distress risk and compresses EV/EBITDA. Matching on these two within the industry is a risk-based complement to the growth/ROIC recipe, and I'd keep it as a robustness check on whether discount-rate matching adds value beyond industry membership.
proposals.prediction: Median |ln error| no worse than 0.34 overall and below the L3 industry median in at least 2 of 4 years; if it fails to beat the baseline, risk matching adds little beyond industry.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank log_sales 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Sales_L2_margin_growth
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is essentially EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so profitability dispersion is what makes the industry-median EV/Sales so noisy; matching on EBITDA margin should remove most of that error, and growth captures the remaining forward-looking premium. I'd use the broader 2-digit pool here because margin matching needs enough candidates to find genuinely similar-margin peers, and I expect this to be the single biggest improvement over any baseline.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| at least 0.10 lower than the L3 industry-median EV/Sales baseline (0.603), and better in all 4 exploration years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Sales_L3_grossmargin_rnd
proposals.mechanism: For firms whose EBITDA is depressed by heavy R&D or SG&A investment (tech, pharma, software), gross margin and R&D intensity capture long-run profit potential better than current EBITDA margin, and the market capitalizes that potential into EV/Sales. Matching on these within the 3-digit industry targets exactly the firms where EV/EBITDA is unusable or misleading.
proposals.prediction: Beats the L3 industry median EV/Sales in at least 3 of 4 years, with the largest improvement in SIC 28, 35, 36, 73.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank gross_margin 1, rnd_intensity 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Sales_L3_ebitmargin_roic
proposals.mechanism: Operating margin sets how much of each sales dollar becomes earnings, and ROIC sets how much reinvestment is needed to grow those earnings, so together they pin down the value of a dollar of sales. This is the EV/Sales analogue of the value-driver recipe and tests whether return on capital adds information beyond margin alone.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.55 and beats the L3 industry-median EV/Sales baseline in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebit_margin 1, roic 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, EV/EBITDA differences mainly reflect expected growth and the return on reinvested capital, so ranking industry peers on sales growth and ROIC selects firms with similar value-creation prospects. Keeping k large and using the median preserves the robustness of the industry-median baseline while tilting toward economically closer peers; the harmonic mean in the original over-weighted low-multiple peers and biased estimates downward.

proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so the dominant driver of a sales multiple is how much of each sales dollar turns into cash profit. Matching on EBITDA margin and gross margin within a broad 2-digit industry finds peers with similar profit conversion, and the median resists the extreme multiples that the mean in the original recipe let through.

proposals.mechanism: A tight hard band on 1-year growth discarded too many good peers and made the peer set noisy; ranking softly on growth instead keeps the industry anchor while favoring firms with similar growth outlooks. EBITDA margin captures the operating-efficiency position that tends to correlate with durability of cash flows and hence the multiple.

proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, ebitda_margin 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: L3 with EBITDA-margin band (EV/Sales)
proposals.mechanism: Leverage says little about how the market prices a dollar of sales, whereas profitability does; a hard EBITDA-margin band inside the industry ensures every peer converts sales into earnings at a similar rate. Ranking the survivors on gross margin and growth then refines for pricing power and expected expansion, and the median limits outlier influence.

A large k with the median averages out idiosyncratic noise across the many fundamentally similar firms.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.600, beating the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years.

Ranking a broad 2-digit pool on these drivers with a fairly large k and the median avoids the downward bias of the harmonic mean while still tailoring the peer set.

proposals.mechanism: My read of round one is that the ranking ideas were reasonable but the harmonic mean, the small k and the L2-only pool added noise that cost more than the matching gained. A fundamentals-based EV/EBITDA should depend on growth and on return on capital (how much reinvestment each unit of growth needs), so I would keep the L3 industry pool, rank on ROIC and 1-year growth, and take the median of a fairly wide set of 20 so that a few extreme peers cannot drag the estimate. If this still fails to beat the plain L3 median, that tells us within-industry matching on value drivers adds little for EV/EBITDA, and we should stop spending effort on it.

proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is EV/EBITDA times the EBITDA margin, so most of the spread in EV/Sales within an industry comes from differences in margin, not size. ROIC was only a weak proxy for this in Recipe 2. I think this is our most promising direction: rank directly on EBITDA margin, with gross margin as a secondary signal of pricing power, inside the larger L2 pool so there are enough close margin matches, and use the median instead of the mean, which right-skewed sales multiples inflate.

proposals.mechanism: The ±0.1 growth band in Recipe 3 probably cut the peer sets down to small, odd groups and pushed many targets onto the L2 fallback. On top of that, the mean was hurt by extreme multiples. Growth is still the main reason EV/EBITDA differs within an industry, so I would rank on it softly instead of screening on it, add EBITDA margin and size as secondary terms (larger, higher-margin firms are usually lower-risk), and take the median of 15 peers.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.335 and beats the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, ebitda_margin 0.5, log_sales 0.4 | k=15, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Profitability-and-growth L3 peers (EV/Sales)
proposals.mechanism: Leverage (Recipe 4) says little about how many dollars of value each dollar of sales produces. What it does is shift value between debt and equity, and EV already looks through that. I would replace it with the two things that actually set EV/Sales, profitability (EBITDA margin) and growth, keep the L3 pool with an L2 fallback, and use the median, because the trimmed mean of 11 still leaves in too much of the skew.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.580 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.mechanism: Recipe 5 had the right instinct to match on margin, but the narrow L4 groups left too few real margin matches, and the mean of 19 was pulled up by extreme multiples. I would apply a hard EBITDA-margin band of ±5 points within L2, so every peer has economically similar profitability, and then rank on margin, growth and size within that band. If the band leaves too few firms, the fallback relaxes it to L2 alone and then to the whole market, still ranking on margin. This is a stronger test of the margin hypothesis than Proposal 2.

proposals.mechanism: Capex intensity matters for EV/EBITDA because EBITDA overstates free cash flow for firms that spend heavily on capital, so investors pay a lower multiple for it. Pairing that with size (Recipe 6) was close to baseline. I would swap size for growth, since growth is what justifies the reinvestment, widen k to 20, and use the median instead of the harmonic mean, which systematically pulls estimates down toward low-multiple peers.

Matching on growth, ROIC and capex intensity inside a 2-digit industry gives a large pool of fundamentally similar peers. A median over 20 peers removes the downward bias of the harmonic mean and the effect of outliers.

Peers from the same 3-digit industry (sharing risk and cyclicality) that are closest in recent growth and ROIC should therefore share the target's multiple most closely.

proposals.name: EBITDA_L3_capex_growth
proposals.mechanism: EBITDA ignores the reinvestment needed to sustain it, so firms with heavy capex convert less EBITDA into free cash flow and deserve lower multiples unless that capex funds growth. Matching within an industry on capex intensity and sales growth pairs firms with similar cash conversion and growth outlook.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median error below 0.333 and below the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.357) on FY2016-2019.

proposals.name: EBITDA_L2_size_leverage

A broader 2-digit pool gives enough candidates to match tightly on both size and leverage.
proposals.prediction: Median error no worse than 0.35 in every exploration year and below the Bhojraj-Lee peers baseline (0.380) pooled.

Peers in the same 3-digit industry with similar EBITDA margin and growth should share the target's EV/Sales.

proposals.name: Cross-industry fundamental twins (EV/Sales)
proposals.mechanism: Margin, growth and R&D intensity drive value per dollar of sales, whatever the SIC code. This is the logic of warranted multiples, applied without a linear model. Using a larger peer set across all industries cuts noise, and ranking on margin first lets matching on fundamentals stand in for industry membership.

proposals.name: L3 margin-band peers with trimmed mean (EV/Sales)
proposals.mechanism: Firms in the same 3-digit industry whose EBITDA margins are within ten points of the target's earn similar profit per dollar of sales, so they should carry similar sales multiples. Ranking on growth and size within that band then picks firms with comparable outlooks. A trimmed mean uses more of the peer information than the median while staying robust to outliers.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.57 and beats the L3 industry median EV/Sales baseline in at least 3 of 4 years.

proposals.name: EBITDA_L3_size_profitability_harmonic
proposals.mechanism: Within a 3-digit SIC industry firms share demand cycles, technology and cost structure, so most of the remaining variation in EV/EBITDA comes from scale (size proxies for diversification and lower risk) and the return on capital earned on reinvestment. The harmonic mean aggregates peers' earnings yields, which damps the upward skew of a few high-multiple peers.

proposals.name: EBITDA_L2_growth_reinvestment
proposals.mechanism: EV/EBITDA rises with expected growth and falls with the share of EBITDA that has to be reinvested to keep the business going, so peers matched on recent growth, ROIC and capex intensity should carry similar multiples. Restricting to the 2-digit industry keeps the common sector risk while leaving a pool large enough to match those fundamentals closely.
proposals.prediction: Pooled median error below 0.333 and below the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple baseline (0.357) in at least 3 of 4 years.

proposals.name: EBITDA_crossindustry_fundamentals
proposals.mechanism: Valuation theory implies EV/EBITDA depends on growth, return on capital, reinvestment needs, leverage-related risk and size, whatever the SIC code. Matching on these drivers across the whole market should find economic twins that industry codes miss, especially for conglomerates and firms that are badly classified.

proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times the EBITDA margin, so peers whose margins differ greatly cannot share a sales multiple even inside the same industry. A hard band of ±5 percentage points on EBITDA margin within the 2-digit industry, followed by ranking on margin and growth, removes most of the dispersion that pure industry peers leave in.

proposals.name: Sales_crossindustry_margin_growth
proposals.mechanism: A sales multiple is mostly capitalized profitability and growth: a dollar of revenue is worth more when more of it becomes cash flow and when it is growing. Matching on EBITDA and gross margin, growth and ROIC across all industries prices each sales dollar directly by its economics rather than by its SIC code.

proposals.mechanism: Firms in the same 3-digit industry with similar EBITDA margins, asset turnover and ROIC have the same economic engine: the same profit per sales dollar and the same capital needed per sales dollar, which together set what a dollar of revenue is worth. Trimming the mean guards against peers with temporarily depressed sales.

Using the 3-digit industry fixes business risk and accounting conventions, and ranking on growth and ROIC within it removes the remaining fundamental gap that a plain industry median ignores.

The harmonic mean is the correct average for price ratios (it averages earnings yields) and limits the pull of peers with very high multiples.
